original.Context: Human substantia nigra neurons
original.Assay: IHC; immunoblot; absorption and H-ferritin cross-reactivity controls
original.Specificity: Monoclonal reagent with target-specific controls
original.Review depth: Primary full text
original.Rationale: Human substantia nigra neurons contain FTMT protein. The 2017 study used two postmortem donors without neurological disorders, a monoclonal reagent, absorption controls and an H-ferritin cross-reactivity check. The later study includes control as well as hemorrhage cases.
original.Limitations: Small postmortem normal-donor panel; does not establish treatment toxicity. Normal neuronal protein conflicts with unrestricted reproductive targeting, even when bulk brain RNA is low. This is not evidence of an observed FTMT-directed treatment injury.

original.Context: Human brain white-matter and peripheral axons

original.Limitations: Abstract-level acceptance for conservative exclusion; full reagent controls not independently reviewed. MRP8 aliases for S100A8 excluded. migrations.rationale: Retain through the accepted normal-protein layer, with measured anatomical scope.

original.Context: Human adrenal cortex (Vital); non-tumor vascular smooth muscle also reported
original.Assay: IHC and immunoblot; peptide competition described
original.Specificity: Peptide-raised polyclonal; reported competition controls not shown
original.Review depth: Primary full text
original.Rationale: The 2006 dbpC/contrin study reports normal vascular smooth-muscle and adrenal-cortical staining. Its specimens include non-tumor surgical regions and autopsies; peptide-raised polyclonal antibodies were checked by immunoblot and peptide competition, with controls described but not shown.
original.Limitations: Non-tumor surgical and autopsy samples; not a cardiomyocyte finding. Modern orthogonal confirmation still desirable. The published non-reproductive protein conflicts with unrestricted inclusion. Vascular cells in myocardium must not be relabelled cardiomyocytes. Modern primary HPA records also contain discordant renal, neural and endocrine staining.

migrations.rationale: Retain through the accepted normal-protein layer, with measured anatomical scope.

original.Context: Human kidney tubules and primary patient-derived proximal tubular cells

original.Specificity: Gene-resolved renal protein role in the primary report
original.Review depth: Primary abstract
original.Rationale: The renal-endocytosis study reports CCDC158 protein in kidney tubules and functional evidence in patient-derived proximal tubular cells.
original.Limitations: Abstract-level acceptance for conservative exclusion; patient-derived cells are not a healthy-volunteer panel. Testis/renal isoforms unresolved. A reproductive gene-level label misses a renal protein role. An isoform-specific target would require its own normal-expression and sequence assessment.

migrations.rationale: Retain through the accepted normal-protein layer, with measured anatomical scope.

original.Context: Differentiating normal human epidermal keratinocytes
original.Assay: Endogenous RNA/protein; two antibodies and protein-band mass spectrometry
original.Specificity: Orthogonal endogenous protein identification
original.Review depth: Primary full text and abstract
original.Rationale: The 2021 study shows endogenous RNA and protein in differentiating normal human epidermal keratinocytes, with two antibody preparations and protein-band mass-spectrometry checks. Retinal epithelial cell-line experiments are additional context, not proof of normal retina in vivo.
original.Limitations: In vitro differentiation state; retinal epithelial cell lines do not establish in vivo normal retina expression. Expression is not confined to permitted follicles or reproductive tissues; ordinary epidermal keratinocytes remain non-permitted. Genetic loss of function and killing expressing cells are different interventions.

migrations.rationale: Material normal-tissue finding remains unresolved; block CTA admission and require sequence review without establishing Unsafe. Negative bulk profiles do not resolve assay identity.

original.Context: Human cerebellar Purkinje cells

original.Limitations: Abstract does not settle reagent specificity; no demonstrated target-mediated clinical injury. A neural protein conflict warrants a hold, but the historical antibody result does not establish target-mediated clinical injury or resolve MAGE-family cross-reactivity.

migrations.rationale: Material normal-tissue finding remains unresolved; block CTA admission and require sequence review without establishing Unsafe. Negative bulk profiles do not resolve assay identity.

original.Context: Adult human bladder and spleen; distinguish fetal/placental specimens
original.Assay: Historical PP13 immunoreactivity versus Northern/placental surveys
original.Specificity: Unresolved galectin cross-reactivity and anatomy
original.Review depth: Primary abstracts
original.Rationale: Early PP13 protein work reported extra-placental reactivity, whereas Northern analysis and later placental-galectin work support placental restriction. Adult bladder/spleen observations must be separated from permitted fetal tissues and possible galectin cross-reactivity.
original.Limitations: Adult versus fetal samples and original protein bands require full-paper adjudication. Conflicting assay identity is unresolved; neither a proven unsafe classification nor unconditional inclusion is justified by these abstracts alone.
